WHAT ACTUALLY MATTERS FOR VAN LIFE SPECIFICALLY Solar input ceiling. Not every power station accepts the same maximum solar wattage. If you're running a rooftop array on a van or RV — rather than a small folding panel — check the unit's rated solar input before assuming your panels will actually deliver their full output. This is one of the more common mismatch points in van builds: a well-sized panel array bottlenecked by a power station's lower solar input ceiling. Weight and footprint. Vans and RVs have hard limits on payload and storage space in a way that cabins and homes don't. Portability-focused designs generally trade some capacity-per-dollar for a lighter, more compact form factor — worth weighing directly against your specific rig's available space. Expandability. How you actually recharge matters more than the spec sheet suggests. If you're relying primarily on solar, recharge speed from a wall outlet or generator matters less. If you're moving frequently and topping up from campground power or a generator between stops, faster recharge times translate directly into less downtime.
